A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete, readable main text and Appendices A–B. Text and rendered pages 2–23 match exactly; page 1 differs only in affiliation information, the arXiv stamp, and associated layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer experiments on arithmetic, string manipulation, and maze tasks, including pretrained-model results and mechanistic analyses in Sections 4–6 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Sections 4–6 and Appendix A, including length-generalization measurements, ablations, and attention-head analyses.

M1.justification: The joint-training procedure, main/auxiliary task construction, transformer architectures, output-token loss masking, and pretrained-model finetuning procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic arithmetic, string-manipulation, and maze tasks, including swapped maze-task roles and unrelated auxiliary-task controls. Appendix A adds no coverage relative to v1.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain identical participants: task-only versus joint training, related versus control auxiliary tasks, and RoPE versus NoPE models. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain identical task-length ranges, sampling procedures, model configurations, training schedules, and exact-match evaluation on 1,024 test examples. The ablation and checkpoint-evaluation protocols also match.

E4.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A retain the same analyses of training-length combinations, training instability, positional encoding, individual auxiliary tasks, and attention-circuit sharing. No analysis or case study is added or revised.

E5.justification: Both versions report five initialization seeds for the main experiments, averaging over three seeds in Section 6.1, and three-seed results in Figure 16. Seed displays and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical entries, plotted curves, heatmaps, and reported findings match throughout the main text and appendices. This includes the generalization-gap values in Figure 10 and additional results in Figures 15–19.

T1.justification: Definitions of task length, generalization gap, and circuit-similarity measures are unchanged. Neither version supplies a formal theoretical framework or proofs; Section 7 retains that limitation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims: length generalization transfers between related tasks, also occurs with pretrained models, and correlates with shared attention-head computation.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning task alignment, reusable structure from pretraining, and circuit sharing are unchanged. Both retain the same qualifications about seed instability, lack of formal theory, and applicability beyond simple algorithmic domains.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains identical model specifications, data formats, hyperparameters, optimizer schedules, and computational-resource information, including two RTX 3090 GPUs and approximately 300 machine-hours. No technical or code/data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations throughout the text, and the reference list are unchanged. The positioning relative to length-generalization methods, task hinting, compositional generalization, and circuit-transfer research remains identical.

P1.justification: v2 adds University of Wisconsin-Madison to Dimitris Papailiopoulos's affiliations and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose, terminology, headings, and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The additional affiliation slightly changes author-block spacing and shifts the abstract and introduction on page 1. All figures, tables, captions, and layouts on pages 2–23 are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 updates affiliation metadata and first-page presentation while preserving all scientific arguments, evidence, limitations, and reproducibility details, including both appendices. These administrative edits produce no meaningful change in the paper's overall quality.
